front_blocks.md: What functional group in a monomer indicates that addition polymerisation will occur?

back_blocks.md: A **C=C double bond**. The double bond opens to allow monomers to add on either side, forming a (poly)alkene chain without expelling any small molecule.

cards.front_md: What functional group in a monomer indicates that addition polymerisation will occur?
cards.back_md: A **C=C double bond**. The double bond opens to allow monomers to add on either side, forming a (poly)alkene chain without expelling any small molecule.

front_blocks.md: Addition polymers have functional groups in their polymer backbone.

back_blocks.md: Addition polymers have a **plain carbon chain** as their backbone with no functional groups. Functional groups only appear as side chains (e.g. benzene rings, halogen atoms or -CN groups).

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Addition polymers have functional groups in their polymer backbone.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Addition polymers have a **plain carbon chain** as their backbone with no functional groups. Functional groups only appear as side chains (e.g. benzene rings, halogen atoms or -CN groups).

back_blocks.md: A **copolymer** is a polymer produced when two or more different alkene monomers undergo addition polymerisation together.

cards.back_md: A **copolymer** is a polymer produced when two or more different alkene monomers undergo addition polymerisation together.

front_blocks.md: How can you deduce from a polymer structure that it was formed by condensation polymerisation?

back_blocks.md: Look at the **polymer backbone**. If it contains functional groups such as **ester links** (-COO-) or **amide links** (-CONH-), it was formed by condensation polymerisation.

cards.front_md: How can you deduce from a polymer structure that it was formed by condensation polymerisation?
cards.back_md: Look at the **polymer backbone**. If it contains functional groups such as **ester links** (-COO-) or **amide links** (-CONH-), it was formed by condensation polymerisation.

front_blocks.md: Monomers containing only C=C double bonds undergo **..........**  polymerisation. Monomers containing -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups undergo **..........**  polymerisation to form a polyamide.

back_blocks.md: Monomers containing only C=C double bonds undergo **addition** polymerisation. Monomers containing -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups undergo **condensation** polymerisation to form a polyamide.

cards.front_md: Monomers containing only C=C double bonds undergo **..........**  polymerisation. Monomers containing -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups undergo **..........**  polymerisation to form a polyamide.
cards.back_md: Monomers containing only C=C double bonds undergo **addition** polymerisation. Monomers containing -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups undergo **condensation** polymerisation to form a polyamide.

front_blocks.md: Acyl chlorides can react with alcohols to form polyesters by condensation polymerisation, expelling HCl.

back_blocks.md: Acyl chlorides (-COCl) react with alcohols (-OH) in condensation polymerisation to form polyesters. HCl is the small molecule expelled at each ester link formed.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Acyl chlorides can react with alcohols to form polyesters by condensation polymerisation, expelling HCl.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Acyl chlorides (-COCl) react with alcohols (-OH) in condensation polymerisation to form polyesters. HCl is the small molecule expelled at each ester link formed.

front_blocks.md: An amino acid contains both -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups. What type of polymer does it form and what is the link called?

back_blocks.md: It forms a **polyamide** by condensation polymerisation. The link formed between adjacent amino acids is called a **peptide link** (amide link), and water is eliminated.

cards.front_md: An amino acid contains both -NH<sub>2</sub> and -COOH groups. What type of polymer does it form and what is the link called?
cards.back_md: It forms a **polyamide** by condensation polymerisation. The link formed between adjacent amino acids is called a **peptide link** (amide link), and water is eliminated.

back_blocks.md: An **addition polymerisation** is a type of polymerisation in which monomers with C=C double bonds join together to form a polymer chain without expelling any small molecule.

cards.back_md: An **addition polymerisation** is a type of polymerisation in which monomers with C=C double bonds join together to form a polymer chain without expelling any small molecule.

front_blocks.md: A polymer with ester links in its backbone is a **..........** . A polymer with a plain carbon-chain backbone and no backbone functional groups is an **..........**  polymer.

back_blocks.md: A polymer with ester links in its backbone is a **polyester**. A polymer with a plain carbon-chain backbone and no backbone functional groups is an **addition** polymer.

cards.front_md: A polymer with ester links in its backbone is a **..........** . A polymer with a plain carbon-chain backbone and no backbone functional groups is an **..........**  polymer.
cards.back_md: A polymer with ester links in its backbone is a **polyester**. A polymer with a plain carbon-chain backbone and no backbone functional groups is an **addition** polymer.
